newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cypriot sticks to story about British AIDS lover.
newsitem.headline: Cypriot sticks to story about British AIDS lover.

text.p: Cypriot fisherman Pavlos Georgiou completed giving evidence to a Cyprus court on Thursday, sticking by his story he never transmitted the deadly AIDS virus to his British lover.
"I always used a condom but Janette never believed it, she thought it was all joke. She never believed I had the AIDS virus in my blood," said Georgiou, 40.
Divorcee Janette Pink, 45, of Basildon in Essex, has accused the father of four of giving her the HIV virus which has developed into Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome.
Georgiou, whose wife died of AIDS and whose youngest of four children is also HIV positive, has denied the charge.
The bearded fisherman says Pink was well aware of his condition before their physical relationship started, but that she did not seem to care.
If found guilty, he could face a sentence of up to two years in jail or a 1,500 Cyprus pound fine, or both.
The couple met when Pink came to settle in Cyprus in 1993 after divorcing her accountant husband.
Georgiou's English-Cypriot wife Martha was dying at the time of AIDS, but Pink says Georgiou told her she was suffering from leukaemia.
Georgiou said at a previous court appearance the only time the two had unprotected sex was when both had consumed considerable quantities of alcohol. He said Pink took the condom off him.
"She thanked me... she really liked sex. She was thirsty for it and wanted it daily," he told the judge, prompting a sarcastic suggestion from prosecutors that he may have been obliging grudgingly.
"Janette was living on her own and had plenty of time. I had four kids to look after," he responded.
Defence will summon two more witnesses before the case is summed up, judicial sources said.
